items.title: How a biodiversity register at CBD COP17 is reclaiming erased Kerala fisher knowledge
items.summary: Nearly a decade after he helped the Kerala State Biodiversity Board (KSBB) document marine life off the Thiruvananthapuram’s coast, marine researcher Robert Panippilla arrived at the UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan with a digital community biodiversity register that is intended to correct a decade-long injustice. The conference, being held from October 19 to 30, 2026, is the first global review of collective progress in implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. “The digital register is a response to the erasure of community knowledge from the marine biodiversity register published by the KSBB in 2017,” Panipilla said, while speaking to TNM at Yerevan in Armenia. According to him, indigenous knowledge was left out of the state’s documentation because scientific experts had failed to identify marine fauna documented by them. Between 2013 and 2015, local fishers led by Robert Panipilla had documented marine biodiversity and the traditional knowledge of local fishing communities in Thiruvananthapuram as part of a KSBB initiative. items.title: Telangana man alleges police assault, cops file FIRs against him
items.summary: Twenty-two-year-old Mohammed Fayaz was walking home on the night of October 2, just past midnight, on the streets of Mahabubnagar in Telangana. When he was a few hundred metres away from his home in Habibnagar, two police constables on patrol duty, Balaram and Kowdi Raju, allegedly beat him up so badly that he started bleeding from the head. The government hospital that treated Fayaz recorded a laceration on the left side of the head, abrasion on the face, and blunt trauma to the chest, neck and leg. But according to the Mahabubnagar I Town police, the injuries are Fayaz’s own fault. When trying to run away from the constables, they say Fayaz “ran into a nearby house, fell down and sustained a bleeding injury to his head.” While there has been no inquiry or action against the constables so far, the police have booked Fayaz for trespassing into Mohammed Kadar’s house in Habibnagar and intimidating him. Except Kadar, who is named as the complainant, told TNM that this never happened and that he was forced by the I Town police to sign the complaint letter. A YouTuber named Azhar Khan, who reported on the incident and protests against the police by Fayaz and his family, was also booked
